newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's king urges restraint to preserve peace.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king urges restraint to preserve peace.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein urged Palestinians and Israelis on Friday to remain calm to stop a renewed eruption of violence sought by anti-peace groups.
King Hussein, in remarks carried by the state news agency Petra from Washington, urged both Palestinians and Israelis to give dialogue a chance in coming talks between them next Sunday.

"We have to give room for dialogue that will begin in the next few days...There is a need for endurance and patience in this phase and not to be led by emotions, knowing that this moves all of us," the king was quoted by Petra as saying.

The monarch hit at "enemies of peace" seeking to exploit raised emotions after Israeli-Palestinian clashes last week killed over 70 people when Israel opened a second entrance to a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.

A resumption of Israeli-Palestinians talks was the main outcome of this week's summit in Washington called by U.S. President Bill Clinton. The king attended along with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.
The monarch criticised Israel for failing to implement its accords with the Palestinians, saying this was falling into the hands of opponents of the Middle East peace process.

"It's as though the enemies of peace are seeing this is their chance as a result of what happened in failure in implementing agreements (Israeli-Palestinian peace accords) until now by the Israeli side," he said.
The monarch said it was "not permissible" for Israel to say it was committed to peace accords signed with the Palestinians while then failing to honour them.

The king also praised Arafat for "shouldering very big responsibilites and adopting a position that has exposed him to a lot of dangers...he has sincerely stood in defence of his people rights on their national soil and for peace."
The king remained in Washington after the end of the summit on Wednesday, holding talks with senior U.S. officials on boosting American economic and defence aid to the kingdom.

The agreement to resume talks despite failure to produce any accords resolving Israeli-Palestinian disputes was seen as a limited achievement that caused Palestinians and many critics to brand the summit a failure.
